name: Reinforcement Learning on Web Interfaces Using Workflow-Guided Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses workflows extracted from demonstrations to constrain reinforcement-learning exploration for interactive web tasks.

name: SheetCopilot: Bringing Software Productivity to the Next Level through Large Language Models
notes: The contribution was reviewed from the retained paper abstract. The original Windows/Excel implementation is identified in the separately retained project README; the later Ubuntu evaluator is not treated as a paper result.
summary: Introduces SheetCopilot, an agent that steers spreadsheet software via atomic virtual APIs, along with a 221-task spreadsheet manipulation benchmark.

name: SteP: Stacked LLM Policies for Web Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SteP dynamically composes specialized web-action policies through a stack that records the active chain of policy calls. It studies this control structure across WebArena, MiniWoB++, and CRM workflows.

name: InstructExcel: A Benchmark for Natural Language Instruction in Excel
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. This is an application-specific automation benchmark grounded in recorded Excel user actions. Its execution interface is OfficeScripts, so it is adjacent rather than a visual GUI navigation benchmark.
summary: Introduces InstructExcel, a benchmark for generating Excel OfficeScripts from natural-language requests, built using scripts recorded from user actions and a collection of existing spreadsheets.

name: ProAgent: From Robotic Process Automation to Agentic Process Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces ProAgent, an LLM-based agent that builds automation workflows from human instructions and coordinates specialized agents during workflow execution.

name: MobileAgent: enhancing mobile control via human-machine interaction and SOP integration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines operating-procedure context with user interaction to guide mobile task automation and handle personalized or sensitive requests.

name: PPTC-R benchmark: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Large Language Models for PowerPoint Task Completion
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. The benchmark directly concerns PowerPoint task automation but executes through APIs, so it remains adjacent.
summary: Benchmarks robustness of API-based PowerPoint completion under sentence-level, semantic, and multilingual instruction perturbations and changes to the available API set.

name: WorkArena: How Capable Are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract.
summary: Introduces enterprise web tasks on ServiceNow and BrowserGym interfaces for evaluating browser-based agents.

name: Prompt2Task: Automating UI Tasks on Smartphones from Textual Prompts
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Prompt2Task converts textual goals or procedures into smartphone UI automation using agents for intent interpretation, external-information handling, and execution. User feedback and accumulated task knowledge support subsequent task generation and operation.

name: FlowMind: Automatic Workflow Generation with LLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: FlowMind generates API-based workflows from user requests for process automation and presents workflow descriptions that users can inspect and comment on.

name: Automating the Enterprise with Foundation Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: ECLAIR uses multimodal foundation models to automate enterprise workflows from natural-language descriptions, with initial studies of workflow understanding and completion.

name: SmartFlow: Robotic Process Automation using LLMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents SmartFlow, which converts visible GUI elements into text for language-model action planning and executes the plan through a scripting engine. A collection of enterprise applications evaluates adaptation to different layouts and tasks.

name: WONDERBREAD: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Foundation Models on Business Process Management Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The demonstrations were rehearsed, so their completion rate is not a zero-shot human performance estimate.
summary: Introduces WONDERBREAD, a benchmark pairing human WebArena workflow demonstrations with screen recordings, action logs, and written procedures. Six evaluation tasks cover documentation, knowledge transfer, and process improvement beyond end-to-end execution.

publication.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

name: Spider2-V: How Far Are Multimodal Agents From Automating Data Science and Engineering Workflows?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Benchmarks multimodal agents on data-science and engineering workflows involving enterprise applications, code, and GUI operations in real computer environments.

name: IDA: Breaking Barriers in No-code UI Automation Through Large Language Models and Human-Centric Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: IDA helps business users create web UI automation through guided demonstrations, a semantic programming model, and a teaching-oriented interface. A prototype user study examines automation creation with enterprise applications by users without programming backgrounds.

name: Agent Workflow Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Agent Workflow Memory extracts reusable task routines and selectively supplies them to guide later web actions. It studies both offline workflow induction from training examples and online induction from test experience on Mind2Web and WebArena.

name: Infogent: An Agent-Based Framework for Web Information Aggregation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its evaluation includes both API-driven access and interactive visual browser access.
summary: Infogent separates navigation, extraction and aggregation for web information gathering, including browser interaction through webpage screenshots.

name: WorkflowLLM: Enhancing Workflow Orchestration Capability of Large Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: WorkflowLLM builds WorkflowBench from application API workflows and synthetic queries, then trains WorkflowLlama to generate multi-application workflows.

name: ScribeAgent: Towards Specialized Web Agents Using Production-Scale Workflow Data
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies fine-tuning open language models on production web-workflow traces, including training choices for specialized web agents.

name: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Simulates a software-company workplace to evaluate agents on professional tasks involving websites, programs, files, and coworker communication.

name: Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Interactive LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: LOOP trains interactive digital agents with reinforcement learning in stateful, multi-app environments where tasks are performed through API calls.

name: Towards Enterprise-Ready Computer Using Generalist Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes the CUGA enterprise-agent development process, emphasizing iterative evaluation, failure analysis, and refinement on software-task benchmarks.

name: ScienceBoard: Evaluating Multimodal Autonomous Agents in Realistic Scientific Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ScienceBoard combines an interactive environment with professional scientific software and 169 human-curated tasks in areas including biochemistry, astronomy, and geoinformatics. It evaluates computer-use agents on visually rich research workflows and analyzes their execution limitations.

name: WorkForceAgent-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLM-based Web Agents via Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses rule-based rewards for output structure and action correctness to train reasoning for enterprise web navigation.

name: macOSWorld: A Multilingual Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: macOSWorld provides 202 interactive tasks across 30 applications, with instructions and operating-system interfaces in five languages. It evaluates GUI agents on macOS workflows and includes a separate subset for deception-attack testing.

name: BIMgent: Towards Autonomous Building Modeling via Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: BIMgent plans software-specific workflows and executes GUI actions for building-information modeling. It evaluates multimodal building design and reconstruction tasks in professional authoring software.

name: AppAgent-Pro: A Proactive GUI Agent System for Multidomain Information Integration and User Assistance
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Proposes a proactive GUI assistant that gathers information across domains in response to user requests and anticipated information needs.

name: AppCopilot: Toward General, Accurate, Long-Horizon, and Efficient Mobile Agent
notes: Trace reuse assumes stable layouts and fixed tasks. The described function-call routes are user-selected, and coordinate calibration depends on valid detected widgets. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (4.2 OCR/OR Region Localization; 4.2.2 Coordinate Calibration; 4.3 Multi-Agent Voting; 5.2 Task Decomposition; 6.2 Experience Reuse; 6.3 Function Calling).
summary: Describes a mobile-agent stack combining region-based coordinate correction, hierarchical task planning, multi-agent voting, and reuse of successful interaction traces.

name: Are LLM Agents the New RPA? A Comparative Study with RPA Across Enterprise Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison covers three enterprise RPA challenges.
summary: Compares an agent using computer interfaces with UiPath RPA on enterprise data entry, monitoring, and document extraction, measuring speed, reliability, and development effort.

name: MAS-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Shortcut-Augmented Hybrid Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MAS-Bench evaluates mobile agents that combine GUI actions with APIs, deep links, and reusable scripts. Its 139 tasks across 11 apps test use of 88 predefined shortcuts as well as the ability to generate new reusable workflows.

name: Agentic Lybic: Multi-Agent Execution System with Tiered Reasoning and Orchestration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported result is from evaluation on OSWorld.
summary: Introduces Agentic Lybic, a desktop automation system that routes tasks among GUI, code, and decision-support workers using a finite-state machine and evaluator.

name: Flash-Searcher: Fast and Effective Web Agents via DAG-Based Parallel Execution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Flash-Searcher, a parallel agent framework that organizes dependent subtasks as a graph and runs independent paths concurrently; it is evaluated on deep-search benchmarks.

name: SCUBA: Salesforce Computer Use Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SCUBA evaluates enterprise UI navigation and CRM workflows with 300 task instances derived from Salesforce user interviews. Salesforce sandbox execution and milestone-based assessment support comparisons between zero-shot agents and agents given demonstrations.

name: ALLOY: Generating Reusable Agent Workflows from User Demonstration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The study involved 12 participants performing complex web tasks.
summary: Introduces ALLOY, which turns user demonstrations into editable, reusable workflows for LLM-based web agents carrying out preference-dependent tasks.

name: ReUseIt: Synthesizing Reusable AI Agent Workflows for Web Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported task results cover fifteen repetitive tasks; the user study involved nine people.
summary: Introduces ReUseIt, which synthesizes reusable web-agent workflows from successful and failed attempts and adds guards to detect and fix execution errors.

name: PolySkill: Learning Generalizable Skills Through Polymorphic Abstraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Reported evaluations include seen and unseen websites and Mind2Web.
summary: Introduces PolySkill, which separates a web-agent skill's goal from its execution so agents can learn and reuse skills across websites.

name: Agent Data Protocol: Unifying Datasets for Diverse, Effective Fine-tuning of LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Browsing is one of several task domains covered by the protocol and its evaluations.
summary: The agent data protocol (ADP) provides a shared format for agent training data across browsing, tool use, coding, and other tasks, including web agent workflows.

name: UI-CUBE: Enterprise-Grade Computer Use Agent Benchmarking Beyond Task Accuracy to Operational Reliability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-CUBE evaluates 226 tasks ranging from individual controls to copy-paste and enterprise workflows. Interface variations, multiple resolutions, and application-state validation support diagnosis of operational reliability beyond task accuracy alone.

name: Using GUI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-EDA collects more than 2,000 screenshot-answer-action pairs from engineers working across five CAD tools and five physical domains. The accompanying benchmark evaluates more than 30 GUI agents on specialized electronic-design workflows.

name: ShowUI-Aloha: Human-Taught GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Transforms human screen recordings and input events into annotated demonstrations used by planning and execution components for GUI tasks.

name: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Terminal-Bench 2.0 benchmarks agents on 89 workflow-inspired tasks in computer terminal environments, with a distinct environment, human solution and verification tests for each task.

name: EntWorld: A Holistic Environment and Benchmark for Verifiable Enterprise GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces EntWorld, an enterprise GUI benchmark built by deriving task logic from database schemas. Long workflows across enterprise domains are assessed with deterministic SQL-based state checks rather than screenshot similarity alone.

name: From Struggle to Success: Context-Aware Guidance for Screen Reader Users in Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces AskEase, an on-demand assistant that combines contextual information to provide screen-reader-friendly computer-use guidance. A study with screen-reader users evaluates task completion and perceived workload while preserving human control of the interaction.

name: When Benign Inputs Lead to Severe Harms: Eliciting Unsafe Unintended Behaviors of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: AutoElicit iteratively revises benign instructions using execution feedback to surface harmful unintended actions by computer-use agents in OS workflows.

name: A Trajectory-Based Safety Audit of Clawdbot (OpenClaw)
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Audits Clawdbot safety through logged action and tool-call trajectories across local execution and web-mediated workflows, using automated and human review.

name: EmbeWebAgent: Embedding Web Agents into Any Customized UI
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EmbeWebAgent embeds agent access into existing web applications through frontend observations and a page-specific function registry. Its workflow combines GUI primitives, composite actions and MCP tools, demonstrated in a live interface.

name: Web Agents Should Use Typed Actions Instead of Click-Based Browsing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Proposes web verbs as typed actions for web agents, exposing operations with structured inputs, outputs and conditions so agents can compose auditable workflows.

name: AgentOS: From Application Silos to a Natural Language-Driven Data Ecosystem
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Proposes Personal Agent Operating System (AgentOS), with a natural language or voice portal and an Agent Kernel that coordinates agents and tasks in place of a GUI desktop.

name: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.

name: Towards Automated Crowdsourced Testing via Personified-LLM
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces PersonaTester, a framework that gives LLM agents tester personas to vary their exploration and interaction habits during automated crowdsourced GUI testing.

name: CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CUA-Suite combines continuous expert desktop demonstrations in VideoCUA with the UI-Vision evaluation benchmark and GroundCUA grounding data. Screen recordings, cursor traces and layered annotations support study of temporal behavior and professional software workflows.

name: GPA: Learning GUI Process Automation from Demonstrations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents demonstration-based GUI process replay with Sequential Monte Carlo localization and readiness checks. GPA executes the learned workflow locally and can serve as the GUI execution component of an agent using MCP or CLI tools.

name: MAESTRO: Adapting GUIs and Guiding Navigation with User Preferences in Conversational Agents with GUIs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces MAESTRO, a conversational GUI system that remembers user preferences, adapts interface options, and guides backtracking in multistep booking decisions.

name: ClawBench: Can AI Agents Complete Everyday Online Tasks?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces ClawBench, 153 everyday tasks on production websites in 15 categories; an interception layer blocks each final submission so bookings, purchases and job applications are scored without side effects.

name: MobiFlow: Real-World Mobile Agent Benchmarking through Trajectory Fusion
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MobiFlow, a mobile-agent evaluation framework that fuses task trajectories into a state graph for dynamic interaction with third-party apps and measures task outcomes.

name: Agentic Compilation: Mitigating the LLM Rerun Crisis for Minimized-Inference-Cost Web Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports evaluation on data extraction, form filling, and fingerprinting tasks.
summary: Proposes Compile-and-Execute, which turns a sanitized DOM into a reusable JSON workflow so repetitive browser tasks can run without further model queries.

name: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HealthAdminBench with GUI environments for an electronic health record, payer portals and fax handling. Expert-defined administrative tasks are decomposed into verifiable subtasks to compare local progress with end-to-end workflow completion.

name: Mobile GUI Agent Privacy Personalization with Trajectory Induced Preference Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its reported results use the authors' Privacy Preference Dataset.
summary: Proposes Trajectory Induced Preference Optimization (TIPO) to train mobile GUI agents for differing user privacy preferences across structurally different task trajectories.

name: Towards Scalable Lightweight GUI Agents via Multi-role Orchestration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces LAMO, a training framework for a lightweight GUI agent that can execute tasks alone or serve as an action executor alongside planners in multi-agent workflows.

name: AgentClick: A Skill-Based Human-in-the-Loop Review Layer for Terminal AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent supervision interface: the browser UI is for human review of terminal agents; the abstract does not claim that those agents operate graphical interfaces.
summary: AgentClick gives terminal-based agents a browser review interface for plans, drafts, execution traces and editable memory. A local server and skill plugin let users inspect proposed actions and provide structured feedback.

name: AutomationBench
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces AutomationBench, a benchmark for agents coordinating business workflows across applications through REST APIs, including endpoint discovery and policy adherence.

name: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: PlayEval measures whether generated GUI applications remain logically playable, using PlayTester to execute task-oriented GUI playthroughs. PlayCoder closes the loop between repository-aware generation, interactive testing and targeted code repair.

name: WindowsWorld: A Process-Centric Benchmark of Autonomous GUI Agents in Professional Cross-Application Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Desktop use is explicit; no additional operating-system claim is inferred solely from the benchmark name.
summary: Introduces WindowsWorld for professional workflows spanning multiple desktop applications, with generated tasks refined through human review. Intermediate subgoals support process-oriented evaluation of cross-application reasoning and execution efficiency.

name: X-OmniClaw Technical Report: A Unified Mobile Agent for Multimodal Understanding and Interaction
notes: The report presents demonstrations. Its behavior-cloning component captures runtime skills; it does not establish policy-weight imitation training, and literal trace replay is described as future work. No general benchmark result or release completeness is inferred. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (2 Framework; 3 Omni Perception; 4 Omni Memory; 5.1 Omni Action in App Ecosystem; 5.2 Trajectory Cloned Execution).
summary: Describes an Android agent architecture combining multimodal perception, working and personal memory, hybrid XML/visual grounding, and reusable skills captured from user interactions.

name: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: LongMemEval-V2 asks memory systems to recover environment knowledge from long web-agent histories for question answering. Its AgentRunbook variants contrast indexed knowledge pools with coding-agent retrieval from stored trajectory files.

name: SaaS-Bench: Can Computer-Use Agents Leverage Real-World SaaS to Solve Professional Workflows?
notes: The complete retained official abstract and cached official README were reviewed.
summary: SaaS-Bench evaluates browser agents on professional workflows across self-hosted applications. Weighted checkpoints measure task completion and partial progress, with application-state checks and configured content judges documented in the official harness.

name: Claw-Anything: Benchmarking Always-On Personal Assistants with Broader Access to User's Digital World
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Claw-Anything benchmarks persistent personal assistance across activity histories, backend services and integrated GUI/CLI interaction. Its simulated event histories introduce irrelevant or conflicting context, and a separate generation pipeline supplies training environments.

name: Anchor: Preventing Artifact Drift for Reliable Agent Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The shared verifier scores end-state business correctness across several agent harnesses.
summary: Anchor builds ERP-Bench by generating procurement and manufacturing tasks with shared state verifiers for evaluating browser and computer-use agents.

name: GUI Agents for Continual Game Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. GUI agents actually load and play browser-game builds, providing an executable interface-testing signal for game-code generation; the central application remains game development.
summary: PlaytestArena evaluates generated browser games using expected in-play behaviors adjudicated by GUI agents. Play2Code pairs a coding agent with a rubric-blind GUI playtester whose interaction traces and feedback guide iterative refinement, with a separate final judge.

name: BlueFin: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Financial Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces BlueFin, a benchmark and evaluation framework for agents handling professional finance spreadsheet workbooks through synthesis, manipulation, and comprehension tasks.

name: Multi-Agent Computer Use
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MACU represents computer-use objectives as a dependency graph whose manager dispatches parallel subagents and revises tasks as new information arrives. Desktop and web experiments examine coordination, information handoff and task-completion time.

name: Context-Aware Workflow Decomposition for Automated Mobile UI Annotation Using Multimodal Large Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The experiments use expert-annotated screens from MUIAnno.
summary: Studies staged prompting for automated mobile UI element annotation, comparing workflow depths and element groupings on expert-annotated MUIAnno screens.

name: DeskCraft: Benchmarking Desktop Agents on Professional Workflows and Human-in-the-Loop Collaboration
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DeskCraft evaluates professional desktop workflows and human-agent collaboration through mid-execution clarification, interruption and post-completion feedback. Its tasks cover creative applications and expose difficulties in long-horizon execution and proactive clarification.

name: MedCUA-Bench: A Screenshot-Only Benchmark for Clinical Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MedCUA-Bench evaluates screenshot-only clinical interface workflows using paired intent- and step-level goals. It combines reconstructed medical interfaces with completion and clinical-safety checks, and separately reports results on a real OpenEMR system.

name: CLI-Anything: Towards Agent-Native Computer Use
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent computer-interface architecture: the described application command harnesses concern computer operation, but no GUI execution or comparative benchmark result is established in the abstract.
summary: CLI-Anything argues for application interfaces built around structured commands, explicit state and execution feedback. It describes transforming existing software into command-line harnesses and organizing that approach through CLI-Hub.

name: Demo2Tutorial: From Human Experience to Multimodal Software Tutorials
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Demo2Tutorial, which turns recorded software interactions into multimodal tutorials with task graphs and reports benefits for GUI-agent planning.

name: Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval extracts reusable sub-procedures from completed web trajectories and represents them as paired text and code. Skills are retrieved against both the current webpage state and the task goal at intermediate execution steps.

name: AppAgent-Claw: CLI Is All You Need for GUI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces AppAgent-Claw, which records demonstrated GUI workflows as reusable OpenClaw skills, locates visual targets during replay and checks intended on-screen effects.

name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.

name: WeaveBench: A Long-Horizon, Real-World Benchmark for Computer-Use Agents with Hybrid Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WeaveBench requires agents to combine GUI, command-line and code operations within long tasks on an Ubuntu desktop. A trajectory-aware judge checks deliverables and interaction evidence, including shortcut behavior that outcome-only grading can miss.

name: WebChallenger: A Reliable and Efficient Generalist Web Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebChallenger builds a hierarchical DOM-derived page representation for selective observation, reusable site maps and compound actions. The framework combines these mechanisms without model fine-tuning and evaluates generalization across multiple web-agent benchmarks.

name: Workflow-GYM: Towards Long-Horizon Evaluation of Computer-use Agentic tasks in Real-World Professional Fields
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Workflow-GYM evaluates long GUI workflows in professional software rather than isolated interface actions. Its analysis examines failures such as omitted stages, accumulated errors and goal drift during specialized end-to-end work.

name: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: PhoneHarness routes phone workflows across GUI actions, device-side commands and host tools while retaining auditable execution traces. Its accompanying benchmark checks observable task side effects, separating mixed-action execution from plausible final-answer generation.

name: LLM-as-Code: Agentic Programming for Agent Harness
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Computer use appears as a case study of a general agent architecture.
summary: Proposes Agentic Programming, where code controls agent loops and invokes LLM-as-Code for reasoning; a computer-use case study examines long visual action sequences.

name: MyPCBench: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MyPCBench tests personal-assistant tasks on a Linux desktop with simulated web applications and data for a single fictional persona. A shared computer-and-shell interface enables evaluation of cross-application workflows that depend on personal context and account-like state.

name: Beyond Domains: Reusing Web Skills via Transferable Interaction Patterns
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SkillMigrator, a web agent that turns successful interactions into reusable skills and transfers them between sites by matching page layouts and live element references.

name: SkillHarness: Harnessing Safe Skills for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SkillHarness, a framework for computer-use agents to learn and reuse skills under safety constraints when interactions include prompt injections or pop-ups.

name: ChainWorld: Composing Long-Horizon Desktop Workloads from Atomic OSWorld Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ChainWorld composes compatible atomic OSWorld tasks into multi-objective desktop chains while preserving their evaluators. It compares giving the full sequence at once with revealing goals turn by turn, exposing different state and session-management failures.

name: GUI vs. CLI: Execution Bottlenecks in Screen-Only and Skill-Mediated Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This benchmark matches desktop goals, initial states and final-state verifiers across screen-only GUI and skill-mediated CLI agents. Its experiments separate graphical execution failures from missing CLI skill coverage, including a verifier-guided skill-augmentation condition.

name: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces extended computer-use workflows with realistic artifacts, changing information, hidden state, and partial-progress and safety assessments.

name: SpreadsheetBench 2: Evaluating Agents on End-to-End Business Spreadsheet Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SpreadsheetBench 2, a benchmark of multi-sheet business spreadsheet workflows for agents, covering generation, debugging, and visualization tasks.

name: PPT-Eval: A Benchmark for Computer-Use Agents on PowerPoint Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PPT-Eval, a benchmark of PowerPoint creation and editing tasks for computer-use agents, with rubrics that score partial progress and presentation quality.

name: Plover: Steering GUI Agents through Plan-Centric Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Plover exposes GUI-agent plans and replanning as persistent artifacts that users can inspect and edit during execution. Its planner–executor design supports localized correction through plan edits, language guidance and screenshot-grounded interventions, studied through failure repair and workflow scenarios.

name: DocOps: A Verifiable Benchmark for Autonomous Agents in Complex Document Operations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces DocOps, a verifiable benchmark for agents handling complex digital-document workflows, with analysis of state tracking, semantic checks, and structural edits.

name: SafeFlow: Semantic Information-Flow Control for Blocking Malicious Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Harmful web-agent behavior is one of four evaluated safety settings; SafeFlow addresses multi-agent systems generally.
summary: Introduces SafeFlow, a semantic information-flow defense for multi-agent delegation, evaluated on safety tasks that include harmful web-agent behavior.

name: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a benchmark for long-horizon office-suite agent tasks with labor-time and price signals, plus rubric-based code verifiers.

name: SynChain: Inducing Computer-Use Agent Systems to Construct Their Own Attack Chains
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SynChain, an attack that induces persistent agents to create poisoned skills or memory entries, and CUAChain for evaluating later attack-chain activation.

name: DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?
notes: The paper abstract and official project README were reviewed. The README documents an Ubuntu desktop and GUI action interface and includes LLM-assisted evaluators; this annotation does not assert that every evaluator is deterministic.
summary: DSAgentBench evaluates end-to-end data-science workflows spanning analysis, modeling and visualization inside a real desktop environment. Task evaluators check produced analytical and visual artifacts, while the released interface supports screenshot or accessibility observations and GUI actions.

name: CoAdapt-GUI: Joint Workflow Context and Policy Adaptation for Unseen GUI Applications
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces CoAdapt-GUI, which adapts workflow context and policy from a mobile GUI agent's own rollouts and rewards when it encounters unseen applications.

name: LegacyWorld: Atomicity-Aware Evaluation of GUI Agents for Legacy Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LegacyWorld evaluates Windows GUI workflows under an atomicity criterion: finish correctly or fail without persistent unintended changes. It compares expert prompts with prompts derived from recorded golden paths and separates useful completion, safe failure and non-atomic side effects.

name: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a \$15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces StateM, a stateful runtime with checked transitions and reusable runbooks for long-horizon agents; its reported evaluations use terminal and business tasks.

name: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines environment-grounded training with demonstration-conditioned workflows, and introduces OSWorkerBench for extended office-task evaluation.

name: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Task Model Induction disentangles concurrent activities in screenshot and mouse/keyboard traces, then constructs hierarchical goals and procedural control flow for each task. Evaluation tests reconstruction of observed execution and reuse of derived skills on held-out tasks.

name: Benchmarking General Mobile Assistants in Challenging Real-World Scenarios
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its seven applications are based on open-source projects.
summary: Introduces GMA, a benchmark of 300 mobile-assistant tasks across seven applications, and studies how agent context retention and state tracking affect complex workflows.

name: A Systematic Survey of Agentic Skills: Architecture, Lifecycle, and Security
notes: Adjacent broad survey of procedural agent skills.
summary: Surveys modular agentic skill architectures, skill lifecycles, and security risks in autonomous tool- and interface-using agents.

name: WebWorld: The Browser as a World Model for Self-Improving Web Code
notes: Adjacent browser-backed artifact validation, not a GUI navigation benchmark or original-source recovery. Distinct from WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training.
summary: Uses typed browser interaction contracts to accept web-code improvements only when target progress and previously verified capabilities are preserved. Accepted transitions supply self-improvement data.

name: OmegaUse-SOP: SOP Engineering for Professional Computer Use from Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OmegaUse-SOP converts expert GUI demonstrations into configurable procedures and refines them with domain rules and human input. It records, abstracts, grounds and verifies live execution, with a case study of photovoltaic simulation workflows in PVsyst 7.2.

name: From Interaction Traces to Persistent Skills: Online Evolution for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: An online skill-evolution framework turns GUI interaction traces and evaluator feedback into a versioned library of reusable procedures without updating model parameters. Controlled OSWorld comparisons examine both the benefits of shared procedural memory and its domain-dependent instability under repeated revision.

name: OmniStepBench: Deployment-Aware Agent Evaluation across Modalities and Task Complexity
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces OmniStepBench, a shared-environment benchmark for evaluating multimodal agents on multi-step tasks, tool use, and delivered artifacts under one scoring protocol.

name: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AutoTailor compiles web trajectories into reusable browser-automation APIs, then filters and dynamically revises the capability inventory. WebArena experiments distinguish API-only operation from an agent that can fall back to ordinary reasoning and browser actions.

name: CADWorld: Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon Computer-Aided Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CADWorld evaluates screenshot-and-GUI agents on long FreeCAD workflows, from modeling and assembly to manufacturing and simulation. Executable checks inspect saved engineering artifacts for geometry, constraints, construction structure and downstream state.

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.

name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.

name: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ERPBench evaluates screenshot-only agents in enterprise software using database values to check the business records produced by their actions. It pairs these state-based checks with a harness for human approval and analyzes cases where visible completion masks incorrect persisted data.

name: EconSkills: Studying Skill Transfer and Retrieval for Web Agents on Live Economic Data
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: EconSkills converts verified economic-data browsing traces into parameterized procedures with navigation, verification and recovery guidance. Its evaluation separates known-skill transfer from library retrieval, exposing the limits of approximate matches to new tasks.

name: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: RecreationWorld gives hybrid agents running reference applications to explore and recreate using native GUI controls and coding tools. Its multi-platform benchmark checks interaction-dependent behavior with programmatic and visual assertions, while trajectory-training transfer is evaluated separately.

name: The Hard Part Comes After Search: Benchmarking Web Agents on Synthesizing, Organizing, and Displaying Knowledge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: KNOWS benchmarks browser workflows that retrieve and synthesize information into documents, presentations and spreadsheets. Task-specific evaluators combine deterministic checks with model judgments, distinguishing partial progress from usable end-to-end artifact completion.

name: CUA-SWE: When Computer-Use Agents Meet Visual Software Engineering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces CUA-SWE, a benchmark and execution environment that combines code changes with graphical interaction and visual inspection of running software. Task-specific tests verify repairs and changes whose required information may be available only through the application interface.

name: Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use: Learning Reusable Policies for Reliable and Efficient Execution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Learns reusable computer-use policies that encode stable workflow logic in programs while delegating grounding and state checks to neural models. Policy iteration executes variants, diagnoses failures, revises the program, and adds verification before state-changing actions.

name: When to Compile a Computer-Use Agent? Measuring Payback and Making Compilation Decisions for Token Efficiency
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces PACE, a protocol and online decision rule for deciding when repeated GUI procedures are worth compiling into programs. It accounts for failed compilation attempts, measured per-use savings, uncertain reuse, and execution costs under an explicit cumulative budget.

name: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces TeleTune, which edits a textual skill library using held-out action prediction on offline software-use logs with missing goals or interleaved tasks. The learned workflows also guide retrieval of demonstrations for subsequent web-agent execution.

name: Work2Skill: Capturing Human GUI Experience for Reusable Agent Skill Induction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Aligns human screen recordings, input events, and accessibility information to derive reusable workflow skills from desktop demonstrations.

summary: Introduces EvoWeb, a benchmark for coding agents that extend web applications through dependent requests; a multimodal web agent checks each version in a live browser.
